title: Keevash, The existence of designs II: Lemma e|E (two-sided) and the thinning probability of the nibble
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two probabilistic estimates in the random algebraic template of P. Keevash, "The existence of designs II" (arXiv:1802.05900), as explicit finite-N inequalities. (1) DesignsII.TParams.lemma_e_E (Lemma 3.6 e|E with Remark 3.7(i), two-sided): in the template space conditioned on the values of the colours at a set U of fixed vertices, a copy φ meeting U in at most r−1 vertices, whose revealed values are F-linearly independent, passes the tests of colour j with probability between (1−δ)ρ₀(k) and ρ₀(k)/(1−δ), where δ = (q²+q|U|)/N < 1 and ρ₀(k) = N^(r−q) z^(−C(q,r)) ((q−r)!/q!)^C(q,r) |𝒜|^(−1) k/N_act. (2) DesignsII.TParams.thinning_probability (the computation of P(φ ∈ Φ') in the proof of Lemma 3.9 nibble): for families C_i (i < m) of copies of pairwise distinct colours, with covering masses μ_i = ∑_{x∈C_i} P(x passes) ≤ 1, thinning parameters q_i ∈ [0,1] with μ_i q_i = t for all i, and independent thinning coins whose event for the covering pattern w has probability ∏_i (1 − w_i q_i), the probability that the realised covering pattern's coin succeeds is (1−t)^m up to 2^m((∑_i μ_i)² + (m+1)·errMax), where errMax is an explicit maximum, over subsets of the families, of second-order terms (pairs of copies within a family and copies of different families sharing an edge). Both statements are finite-N inequalities valid for all permitted parameters; no asymptotic claim is part of the statements. Mathlib does not contain these results.
